newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates dip in week - Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates dip in week - Freddie Mac.

text.p: Home mortgage rates fell this week as interest rates edged lower on signs that inflation remains under control, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed rate mortgages averaged 8.08 percent in the week ending April 25, down from 8.16 percent last week. Fifteen-year mortgage rates fell to 7.62 percent from 7.71 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates also inched downward to 5.86 percent from 5.89 percent, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.92 percent, the 15-year was 7.43 percent and the adjustable loan 5.74 percent.

"The economy is still strong, but we have not seen signs of inflation in the Consumer Price Index, which has been running fairly consistent at about 3 percent," said Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac's chief economist.
Lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.5 percent on adjustable loans, up from 1.4 percent last week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
